Answer: D
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates situs inversus totalis, characterized by dextrocardia (heart apex pointing to the right) and a left-sided gastric bubble (implied by the mirror-image anatomy), along with the horizontal fissure appearing in the left hemithorax (indicating a morphologic right lung on the left side). These findings of complete situs inversus are the hallmark radiographic feature supporting a diagnosis of Kartagener syndrome when combined with the clinical history.
